messages:
Amy Chen (support): Hey team — Acme is seeing a big spike of 429s and 300–600ms extra p50 latency from APAC customers starting ~03:30 UTC. They reported a burst of requests from a batch job. Sample x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d.
Customer Ops (Acme Inc.): Confirmed. We ran a normal ingestion batch (6k reqs over 60s). Most requests returned 429 or very slow. No change on our side.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: service/routing-service v2026.03.15-87f2 at 03:28 UTC by ci/cd.
Mike Lee (eng-oncall): Thanks. Can we get routing-service + rate-limiter counters for apac region around 03:25–03:35? Start with prometheus query and recent logs.
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): Pasted the routing debug from the node that handled the failing traces.
```
2026-03-15T03:29:12Z routing DEBUG route_decision request_id=req_0a1b2c3d region=apac prefer=region_affinity
available_slots[apac]=0 available_slots[us-west]=12 policy=failover
decision=route_to_us-west-2 reason="region_exhausted"
latency_estimate_ms=28
```
Julia Park (eng-sre): Rate limiter counters (apac):
```
rate_limit_apac.requests_total +42000 (03:25–03:31)
rate_limit_apac.throttled_total +6200
rate_limit_us-west.requests_total +18000
rate_limit_us-west.throttled_total +120
```
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): Runtime logs show a cascade: requests routed out-of-region -> us-west auth checks call vault in us-west -> token introspect extra roundtrip 100–250ms -> per-worker request queue grows -> local APAC queue fills -> hard 429s from apac limiter.
Amy Chen (support): So cascade: exhausted APAC capacity -> failover -> cross-region auth adds latency -> queues backpressure APAC -> 429s. Does that match?
Mike Lee (eng-oncall): Yes. Two follow-ups: 1) why did apac available_slots go to 0 so fast? 2) why wasn't there a gradual fallback or queuing policy to smooth bursts?
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): On 1) autoscaler didn't kick in because the burst was short-lived and our scale-up window is 2m. On 2) policy is strict_region_affinity with immediate failover when region capacity=0. That minimizes cost but is brittle under sudden spikes.
Customer Ops (Acme Inc.): We need a short-term fix — can you stop the 429s and reduce latency? We can't change our client's retry logic quickly.
Julia Park (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations we can try (short timeline):
- push a soft-affinity rollout to routing-service so requests prefer local region but allow gradual overflow (max 20% cross-route per minute).
- temporarily increase APAC reserved capacity (manual scale-up/top-up override) for the next 30m.
- tweak rate-limiter to favor in-flight handoff instead of hard 429 for short bursts (e.g., short queue with jittered retry headers).
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): I can change routing policy flag to soft_affinity and reduce failover aggressiveness. Command to flip (will cause update across routing fleet):
```
# update via infractl
infractl routing set-policy --env prod --region apac --policy soft_affinity --overflow-rate 0.2
```
Mike Lee (eng-oncall): I will request a capacity top-up for APAC now. Julia, can you check the risk of making soft_affinity live (+ rollback plan)?
Julia Park (eng-sre): Risk: Slight increase in cross-region egress and cost; rollback: revert policy to strict_affinity via same infractl command. I'll keep an eye on rate limiter metrics.
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): Also adding a small optimization: when routing to non-local auth cluster, reuse cached introspection results for 5s for internal service tokens. Patch and hot-redeploy to routing-auth-proxy.
```
# minimal patch
cache.ttl = 5s
cache.keys = ["internal-service-token-*"]
```
Amy Chen (support): I'll message Acme with a play-by-play and ask them to add jitter/linear backoff on retries for now. Also asking them to pause big batch jobs if possible for the next 20–30m.
Customer Ops (Acme Inc.): We'll pause the nightly ingestion job. Thanks.
deploy-bot: rollout started: routing-service policy update (soft_affinity) by infractl at 03:39 UTC.
Mike Lee (eng-oncall): APAC capacity top-up: increased reserved GPU pool by 2 nodes at 03:40 UTC. Watch pods and queue depth.
Julia Park (eng-sre): Watching metrics: throttled_apac dropping from +6200 to +300 over 6m. p50 latency for APAC reducing from 420ms to 120ms. Cross-region egress up ~12% but within budget.
Kevin Tran (eng-runtime): Hotfix to routing-auth-proxy deployed 03:45 UTC. Auth latency on cross-region traces dropped ~120ms.
Amy Chen (support): Current status: Customer paused batch, routing-policy flipped, capacity top-up done, auth-cache hotfix in. Can we call this mitigated and keep the thread open for next 24h?
Julia Park (eng-sre): Mitigated. I'll keep an SLO watch and create a follow-up ticket to adjust autoscaler window and add burst-smoothing queue.
Mike Lee (eng-oncall): Owner items:
- Julia: create ticket for autoscale window -> reduce to 30s for APAC (PRIO).
- Kevin: perf review of routing failover to avoid token roundtrips.
- Product/Support: doc for recommended client-side burst best practices (jitter, rate limits).
Amy Chen (support): I'll send ACME a short incident summary and next steps. Closing for now but leaving monitoring. :white_check_mark:
Customer Ops (Acme Inc.): Thanks everyone — much better now.
